Europe Port Congestion Rises Amid Trade & Alliance Shifts
Major European Ports are Experiencing Congestion Challenges
The Three Major Ports Of Antwerp, Hamburg And Rotterdam Are Seriously Congested - sea/ocean freight - News - SDI Logistics
Traders shift to China-Europe freight trains as European port congestion intensifies

paragraphs.text: Recent reporting points to sustained congestion at Rotterdam:
Port of Rotterdam continues to see elevated dwell times — averaging roughly 14 days at RWG and about four days at ECT.
Recent labor actions at Antwerp and Rotterdam have ended or been temporarily paused, though congestion persists, currently averaging two to eight days at Rotterdam.

Persistent congestion at major north European ports — including Rotterdam, Hamburg, and Antwerp — continues constraining capacity by extending vessel turnaround times and reducing effective service frequency.
At several key terminals in Antwerp and Rotterdam, yard utilisation has reached or exceeded 90%, well above the 75% threshold typically associated with severe congestion.
A similar situation is visible at Europe Container Terminals (ECT), Rotterdam where yard space is up to 85 percent full.
Separately, the average waiting time for ships in Rotterdam has been as long as 77 hours.
Traders are beefing up contingency plans such as switching to China-Europe freight trains to deal with congestion at major ports in Europe.
Note: these are web-reported figures, not modelled output from SupermAP tools.
